docs.title: Welcome to my website!
docs.text:
I am a PhD candidate at ECARES at the Université libre de Bruxelles, under the supervision of Estelle Cantillon.

My research interests lie at the boundary between Industrial Organization and Energy and Environmental Economics.

I currently focus on the design of electricity markets to support the energy transition.

In Spring 2026 I visited the Toulouse School of Economics (TSE), hosted by Stefan Ambec in the Environmental Group.

I am on the Job Market this year.

Job Market Paper
docs.text:
Who benefits from the energy transition? Market power and flexibility in retail electricity markets with Elise Viadere (ULB)

Abstract: The energy transition widens intraday spot price spreads — the difference between the most and least expensive hours of the day — raising the value of consumers' flexibility. We study which contracts a monopolist offers to consumers with privately known, heterogeneous flexibility. In equilibrium, the retailer screens consumers by the contracts' price spread and offers a menu of dynamic contracts with different spot price signals. Only the most flexible face the full spot price spread; less flexible consumers face a compressed spread. This distortion increases with the share of flexible consumers. The retailer captures most flexibility gains; low-flexibility consumers retain none.
